en: Mount Mayon in Albay is a highly active stratovolcano famous for its nearly perfect symmetrical cone shape.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward through the Cagayan Valley into the Babuyan Channel.
The Philippine eagle, endemic to Philippine forests, is one of the largest and most powerful eagles globally.
Lake Taal in Batangas is a unique freshwater crater lake located entirely within a much larger volcanic caldera.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features a spectacular limestone karst landscape and flows directly into the sea.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The rare Rafflesia plant, found in Philippine rainforests, produces the largest individual flower on Earth, which smells like rotting meat.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea protects a massive atoll containing hundreds of marine species.
The Philippines experiences a tropical climate with distinct wet and dry seasons, driven by the southwest and northeast monsoons.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao are ancient agricultural structures carved into the mountains using traditional stone-wall building techniques.
The Philippines holds massive global reserves of nickel ore, which is primarily extracted from open-pit mines in Surigao.
The Philippine archipelago comprises 7,641 islands divided into three main geographical divisions: Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao.
